title: AWS temporary key ID with a lowercase body byte, inside the documented API pattern
summary: An ASIA-prefixed 20-character identifier whose body has one lowercase letter where the documented example has an uppercase letter or digit. Shape only; no fixture value is recorded.
rationale: The generic wrong-alphabet reasoning assumes the provider never issues the character. For this family no page lists the issued bytes. The STS Credentials type gives AccessKeyId the pattern [\w]*, which includes lowercase letters, and the GetAccessKeyInfo input is described as allowing any upper- or lowercase letter or digit. Those are request and response type patterns, so they do not show that lowercase bytes are issued either; the uppercase-only reading rests on a documented example and the shape of several scanner rules.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved: the provider patterns for AccessKeyId accept lowercase letters and no page says which bytes are issued, so neither a flag nor a no-flag outcome follows. Would resolve: a provider statement of the issued alphabet, or a maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer.

sources.supports: AccessKeyId input: allows any upper- or lowercase letter or digit

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
